title: Joe Burrow Named AFC Offensive Player of the Week Again
subheadline: Cincinnati's quarterback went 16 of 18 after halftime in Baltimore, and the honors followed. Next up is a home game against Tennessee.

body: Joe Burrow needed only one half in Baltimore to put together one of the best stretches of his career. After being held scoreless in the first half, the Bengals scored all 35 of their points after the break, and Burrow threw all four touchdowns.
That performance in Week 7 on Oct. 25 earned him AFC Offensive Player of the Week, the ninth time he has won the award, and the FedEx Air Player of the Week vote, announced Oct. 28.
## A second half to remember
Burrow finished 22 of 30 for 292 yards with no interceptions. The second half did the damage: he completed 16 of 18 passes for 249 yards and spread his four scores among four different receivers.
No other quarterback has thrown four touchdown passes in a single half this season, according to the Bengals.
## Burrow's season so far

The first overall pick in the 2020 draft is in his seventh season, and he is playing some of his sharpest football. Through six games he has 1,653 passing yards, 15 touchdowns, three interceptions and a 110.4 passer rating. Those 15 touchdown passes are the most he has thrown through six games of any season.

Accuracy and timing remain the core of his game. He completes passes in tight windows, keeps the ball moving to every part of the field and rarely gives it away. Last year he became the third-fastest player in NFL history to reach 150 touchdown passes.
For Cincinnati, he is the reason a 4-2 start feels sustainable. The Bengals have won two straight, and their passing game gives them a chance in any shootout.

title: Victor Wembanyama Drops 43 as Spurs Beat the Timberwolves
subheadline: San Antonio's star added seven rebounds and six blocks on Halloween night, his 10th regular-season game with at least 40 points.

body: Victor Wembanyama spent Halloween night doing things at both ends of the floor that no one else in the NBA can.

The [Spurs center](/players/victor-wembanyama/) scored 43 points on 17-of-34 shooting, grabbed seven rebounds, blocked six shots and handed out four assists as San Antonio beat the Minnesota Timberwolves 121-111 on Oct. 31 at Frost Bank Center.
## Another 40-point night

It was the 10th regular-season game of 40 or more points in his career, and the 11th counting the playoffs, according to ESPN. San Antonio trailed by one at halftime, then outscored Minnesota 33-27 in the third quarter and 28-23 in the fourth.
He had help. Dylan Harper added 25 points and six assists, and De'Aaron Fox scored 20. The win was San Antonio's fourth in a row and lifted the team to 4-2.
## Built for both ends
Wembanyama arrived as the first overall pick in 2023 and has grown into the league's most unusual star. He is 22, stands well over seven feet and handles the ball like a wing.

Defense is where he first separated himself. Last season he led the NBA with 197 blocks, an average of 3.1 per game, and became the first unanimous Defensive Player of the Year. He was also the youngest player ever to win it.

He then carried the Spurs deep into the 2026 playoffs, including a Game 7 win over Oklahoma City in the Western Conference finals. The scoring nights are now arriving more often, which makes him harder to plan for every week.

Few players in any sport combine his size, skill and highlight reel. He is the face of a young Spurs team that already reached the conference finals, and he keeps adding new chapters at 22.

title: Gabby Williams Wins Finals MVP as Valkyries Take WNBA Title
subheadline: Golden State beat Atlanta 68-63 at Chase Center for its first championship, in only its second season, behind Williams' record second half.
description: Gabby Williams scored 28 of her 30 points late as Golden State beat Atlanta 68-63 in Game 7 for its first WNBA title. She was named Finals MVP on Oct. 31.
searchIntent: Fans who heard the Valkyries won the title want to know how Game 7 was won and who Gabby Williams is, with a path to her jersey.
body: Gabby Williams had two points at halftime of the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history. She finished with 30, a championship and the Finals MVP award.

The [Valkyries forward](/players/gabby-williams/) scored 28 of her points in the final 20 minutes as Golden State beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 on Oct. 31 at Chase Center. The title is the first in franchise history and came in the team's second season.
## The comeback

Atlanta led 30-24 at the break. Williams then scored 15 points in the third quarter, including Golden State's last 11 of the period, to put the Valkyries ahead 45-44 going into the fourth. ESPN reported that her second half set a Finals record for points in a half.

With the game tied late, she hit a 3-pointer that put Golden State in front for good, and Veronica Burton sealed it with two free throws with 5.1 seconds left. Williams also blocked four shots. Kiah Stokes added 13 rebounds and won her fourth title.
## How she got here

Williams, 30, played in Chicago and Seattle before joining Golden State this season. She averaged 14.4 points and 1.6 steals in 39 regular-season games and finished second in Defensive Player of the Year voting.
She is a two-time All-Star and a two-time All-Defensive selection, and she has played for France on the biggest stages. This was her first WNBA championship.
Her two-way play fits what the Valkyries have been since they arrived. In 2025 they became the first expansion team to make the playoffs in their first year. One season later, they are champions.

A Finals MVP from a franchise's first title is a jersey that carries history. Williams is now the face of the moment that put the Valkyries on top, and Bay Area fans have a new champion to wear.

headline: Sandy Alcantara Stays in Miami as the Marlins Pick Up His $21 Million Option
title: Marlins Keep Sandy Alcantara With His $21 Million Option
subheadline: The 2022 Cy Young winner led the majors in innings in his second year back from Tommy John surgery, and Miami chose to keep its longest-tenured player.
description: The Marlins exercised Sandy Alcantara's $21 million option for 2027 after he led the majors with 214 innings. The 2022 Cy Young winner stays Miami's ace.
searchIntent: Marlins fans want to know whether Alcantara is staying, what the option costs and what his 2026 season looked like, with a path to his jersey.
body: Sandy Alcantara is staying in Miami. On Oct. 30 the Marlins exercised his $21 million club option for 2027 rather than pay a $2 million buyout, keeping the longest-tenured player on the roster in teal for at least one more season.
The move caps a strong comeback year for the [Marlins right-hander](/players/sandy-alcantara/), who was the subject of trade rumors in each of the past two years.
## A workhorse again

The 2026 season was Alcantara's second back from Tommy John surgery, and he looked like himself again. He threw 214 innings, the most in the majors, and made 33 starts with 21 quality starts. He finished with a 3.87 ERA and 153 strikeouts for an 80-82 club.
He also tried something new over the final two weeks, converting all three of his save chances. They were the first saves of his career.
## The face of the franchise
Alcantara, 31, has spent eight seasons with Miami. He has made 202 starts with a 3.69 ERA, and MLB.com notes he holds several franchise records, including innings, strikeouts and quality starts.
His high point came in 2022, when he won the National League Cy Young Award unanimously. He was the first Marlins pitcher to win it.

The option raises the total value of his deal to six years and $75 million. It also makes 2027 his final season of team control. MLB Trade Rumors reported that Miami does not plan to trade him and intends to start him on Opening Day. Whether the two sides talk about an extension is speculation for now.
## Why fans want the Sandy Alcantara jersey

Long careers with one team are rare, and Alcantara has become the steady presence of Marlins baseball through rebuilds and roster turnover. A Cy Young winner who came back from major surgery to lead the majors in innings is easy for fans to rally behind.

headline: David Pastrnak Passes Patrice Bergeron for Third on the Bruins' All-Time Goals List
title: David Pastrnak Passes Bergeron With His 428th Bruins Goal
subheadline: Boston's captain scored on a first-period breakaway against Chicago, and the Bruins rallied from two goals down late to win 5-4 in overtime.
description: David Pastrnak scored his 428th goal on Oct. 31 to pass Patrice Bergeron for third in Bruins history, and Boston beat Chicago 5-4 in overtime at TD Garden.
searchIntent: Fans want to know which record Pastrnak just broke, who is still ahead of him and how the game ended, with a path to his Bruins jersey.
body: David Pastrnak now has more goals for the Boston Bruins than Patrice Bergeron, and only two players in franchise history have more than him.

The [Bruins captain](/players/david-pastrnak/) took a pass from Pavel Zacha and scored on a breakaway at 13:05 of the first period on Oct. 31 against the Chicago Blackhawks at TD Garden. It was his 428th goal for Boston, one more than Bergeron, and it moved him into sole possession of third on the club's all-time list.
## A night that ended in overtime

The milestone was only the start. Chicago led 4-2 midway through the third period before Mason Lohrei scored, and Morgan Geekie tied it with 12 seconds left and the goalie pulled. Elias Lindholm won it 2:32 into overtime, and Michael DiPietro made 37 saves. Boston improved to 10-4-1.
## From the 25th pick to the record book
Boston took Pastrnak 25th overall in the 2014 draft, and he scored his first two NHL goals in January 2015. The goal against Chicago came in his 848th regular-season game.

Since then he has become one of the league's most dangerous shooters. He scored 61 goals in 2022-23 and has put together four straight 100-point seasons. This season he became the 28th captain in team history.

Two Hall of Famers remain ahead of him. Phil Esposito scored 459 goals as a Bruin, 31 more than Pastrnak, and Johnny Bucyk holds the record with 545. Bergeron, meanwhile, will be inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame on Nov. 9.
## Why fans want the David Pastrnak jersey

Pastrnak is the captain, the top scorer and the link between Boston's last great era and its next one. Every goal now adds to a place in franchise history, which gives the No. 88 lasting appeal for Bruins fans.

title: Robert Lewandowski Scores Winner as Chicago Beats Colorado
subheadline: The veteran striker broke a scoreless run with the go-ahead goal and set up another as the Fire won 4-2 heading into Decision Day.
description: Robert Lewandowski came off the bench to score the winner and add an assist as the Chicago Fire beat Colorado 4-2 on Oct. 31, his first goal in nine matches.

body: Robert Lewandowski had gone eight matches without a goal. On Oct. 31 he needed 11 minutes off the bench to end that run and win a match for the Chicago Fire.

The [Fire striker](/players/robert-lewandowski/) replaced Maren Haile-Selassie in the 63rd minute with the score tied 2-2 at Dick's Sporting Goods Park. In the 74th minute he ran onto a pass from Philip Zinckernagel, went around goalkeeper Nicholas Hansen and finished to put Chicago ahead. He then slipped a through ball to Puso Dithejane for the fourth goal in the 88th minute.
## A big road win

Jonathan Bamba scored twice for Chicago, which won 4-2 and reached 55 points. The result ended the Colorado Rapids' 10-match unbeaten run at home. The Fire had already clinched a playoff spot two weeks earlier, so the points help their seeding before Decision Day against the Columbus Crew.
## A legend's first MLS season

Lewandowski, 38, came to Chicago with one of the best résumés in the sport. He played four seasons for Borussia Dortmund, eight for Bayern Munich and four for Barcelona, and he represented Poland for 18 seasons.
His first MLS season has brought plenty of highlights. He had six goals and three assists in his first 16 league appearances, and Chicago has been one of the stronger teams in the East.

His game has always been built on movement in the box and calm finishing, and both were on show in Colorado. He does not need many touches to change a match, which makes him a weapon even in a smaller role.

Few players in MLS history have arrived with his reputation, and he chose Chicago. For Fire fans, the No. 9 is a link to one of the great goal scorers of his generation, and a reminder that their club is a playoff team this fall.
